toolGroups.label: Connect & diagnose
toolGroups.blurb: Confirm Claude can actually see Figma and Chrome before anything else runs.

toolGroups.label: Find & run
toolGroups.blurb: Find any tool or skill by keyword, then run it or load its full instructions, no separate install needed.

toolGroups.label: Choose what to work on
toolGroups.blurb: Set the scope: a whole page, one artboard, or a single inspected element.

toolGroups.label: Score & measure
toolGroups.blurb: Read your current state. The audits return a gauge plus the issue list behind it.

toolGroups.label: Fix everything at once
toolGroups.blurb: Whole-page and whole-frame conversions. Dry-run by default, and they report the score they moved.

toolGroups.label: Fix one thing at a time
toolGroups.blurb: Surgical, per-property edits with a clean one-click revert for each.

toolGroups.label: Undo & history
toolGroups.blurb: Step back out of any bulk change without leaving the conversation.

toolGroups.label: Restyle the live page
toolGroups.blurb: Chrome only. Inject CSS, flip dark mode, and switch on accessibility overlays.

toolGroups.label: Spec Mode
toolGroups.blurb: Turn a design into CSS, tokens, and specs a developer can paste in.

toolGroups.label: Keep the server current
toolGroups.blurb: Check whether a newer MCP server build is available, and pull it in.

toolGroups.label: Escape hatch
toolGroups.blurb: Raw access for anything the tools above do not cover yet.

skillGroups.label: Coded prototypes
skillGroups.blurb: Build a working demo out of a real component library, not styled boxes.

skillGroups.label: Score & triage
skillGroups.blurb: Turn a pile of issues into a ranked list of what to do first.

skillGroups.label: Convert to Lyra
skillGroups.blurb: Set expectations and scope before anything gets rewritten.

skillGroups.label: Spec Mode
skillGroups.blurb: Produce the spec or the CSS a developer can build from.

skillGroups.label: Design ↔ build parity
skillGroups.blurb: Compare what was designed against what actually shipped.

skillGroups.label: Live-page QA
skillGroups.blurb: Catch what only breaks in the real browser.

skillGroups.label: Design-system maintenance
skillGroups.blurb: Feed what you learn back into the system itself.

skillGroups.label: Context & knowledge
skillGroups.blurb: Real context on NICE, its products, and the team, so design and staffing decisions are grounded instead of generic.

skillGroups.label: Customer personas
skillGroups.blurb: Review and prioritize through a specific real customer, not a generic user.

skillGroups.label: General utilities
skillGroups.blurb: Small, standalone tools that are not specific to Figma, Chrome, or NICE.

tools.name: list_targets
tools.title: See what is connected
tools.what: Lists which clients (Figma, Chrome, or both) are live on the MCP hub right now.
tools.benefit: Stops you from waiting on a tool that was never going to reach anything. Always the cheapest first call.
examples: Is Claude connected to my Figma file and Chrome right now?
Before we start, check which NiCE Designer clients are live.
Can you see my browser tab, or only Figma?

tools.name: get_diagnostics
tools.title: Troubleshoot the connection
tools.what: Full health report on the bridge: this process, the hub, connected sessions, recent drop-outs, and a plain-English next step.
tools.benefit: Turns "it just does not work" into a specific thing to click. Run it the moment a tool says nothing is connected.
examples: Nothing is connecting. Figure out why and tell me what to click.
Run diagnostics on the NiCE Designer bridge and explain the result in plain English.
The plugin says connected but your tools fail. Check the connection health.

tools.name: check_libraries
tools.title: Check the design library is linked
tools.what: Verifies the SOL or Lyra library is actually linked to the open Figma file.
tools.benefit: A missing library silently makes every conversion fall back to bundled values. This catches that before you convert anything.
examples: Is the Lyra library actually linked to this Figma file?
Before I convert anything, check that the design library is attached.
Why are my conversions using bundled values? Check the linked libraries.

tools.name: analytics_summary
tools.title: Show my usage
tools.what: Reads this install's local analytics store and reports total events, panel minutes, top tools, top skills, and whether uploading is configured.
tools.benefit: Answers "what am I actually using?" from your own machine, and tells you at a glance whether analytics is recording and reaching the dashboard.
examples: Show me which NiCE Designer tools I use the most.
How many minutes have I spent in the plugin, and is analytics uploading?
What are my top skills this month?

tools.name: list_skills
tools.title: Browse available skills
tools.what: Returns every skill in the catalog: id, title, the question it answers, and who built it.
tools.benefit: Say "run North Star Fox" or "what skills do you have" and Claude finds it by name or topic, no id-guessing.
examples: What skills do you have available through NiCE Designer?
Show me every skill that helps with research.
Which skills were built by other people on the team?

tools.name: get_skill
tools.title: Load a skill's instructions
tools.what: Fetches a skill's full instructions and reference files, from a live copy first or this server's bundled copy as fallback.
tools.benefit: Flip Supercharge on and every skill works immediately, nothing else to install, updates land with no reinstall.
examples: Load the a11y-triage skill and follow it.
Read the full instructions for the lyra-visual-patterns skill before we convert this page.
Pull up the north-star-fox skill so I can see what it does.

tools.name: get_lynn_ui
tools.title: Get the Lynn package
tools.what: Hands over the bundled lynn-ui React package: copies it into a project folder, or returns its files, so a Lynn prototype needs no download.
tools.benefit: Lynn prototypes work in sandboxed sessions that cannot reach the web or this connector's disk, with nothing to clone or build.
tools.ask: Which project folder should lynn-ui be copied into?
examples: Copy the Lynn package into this project so I can build a prototype with it.
The Lynn download is blocked here. Get the package through the connector instead.
What version of lynn-ui is bundled with NiCE Designer?

tools.name: find_capability
tools.title: Find a tool or skill by keyword
tools.what: Keyword-searches every tool AND skill in the catalog at once, including marketplace skills, and returns ranked matches with exactly how to run each one.
tools.benefit: One search instead of guessing which of ~58 tools or 40+ skills covers a vague ask like "something about contrast" or "help with dark mode".
examples: Is there anything in NiCE Designer that helps with color contrast?
Find me a tool or skill for dark mode problems.
I need to hand this to a developer. What could help?

tools.name: get_selection_info
tools.title: What is selected right now
tools.what: Reports the selected Figma layer or the inspected Chrome element, so scope is explicit rather than assumed.
tools.benefit: Guarantees the audit or fix lands on the thing you meant. No silent whole-page conversions when you wanted one button.
examples: What do I have selected right now?
Confirm which element you will audit before you start.
Tell me what the inspected element is on this page.

tools.name: select_page
tools.title: Reset scope to the whole page
tools.what: Clears the inspected element so audits and fixes cover the entire page again.
tools.benefit: One call to zoom back out after drilling into a component.
examples: Zoom back out and audit the whole page again.
Clear the inspected element so the next audit covers everything.
Reset the scope to the full page.

tools.name: start_inspect
tools.title: Start element picking
tools.what: Turns on the extension's inspect mode so the next element you click becomes the scope.
tools.benefit: Point at the thing you care about instead of describing it in words.
examples: Turn on inspect mode so I can click the element I mean.
Let me point at the button I want you to look at.
Start element picking in Chrome.

tools.name: stop_inspect
tools.title: Stop element picking
tools.what: Leaves inspect mode without changing the current selection.
tools.benefit: Gets the picking cursor out of your way so you can use the page normally.
examples: Turn off inspect mode but keep what I picked.
I am done picking elements, stop inspecting.
Leave inspect mode without clearing my selection.

tools.name: focus_node
tools.title: Jump to a layer in Figma
tools.what: Scrolls to and selects a specific node id on the Figma canvas.
tools.benefit: Every audit row becomes clickable: go straight from "issue #14" to the actual layer.
examples: Jump to the layer with the contrast issue in Figma.
Select node 123:456 and scroll to it.
Take me to the first off-token fill you found.

tools.name: screenshot_page
tools.title: Screenshot what you are looking at
tools.what: Captures the current page or artboard as an image Claude can look at directly.
tools.benefit: Lets Claude judge things a token audit cannot see: visual hierarchy, crowding, whether it simply looks wrong.
examples: Take a screenshot of this page and tell me what looks off.
Capture the selected artboard so you can compare it to the live site.
Grab an image of the current view before we change anything.

tools.name: run_full_audit
tools.title: Full compliance score
tools.what: Audits colors, typography, spacing, radius, components and accessibility in one pass and returns an overall 0–100 score with per-domain issue counts.
tools.benefit: One number you can put in front of a stakeholder, plus the exact list of what is dragging it down.
tools.ask: Audit only the current selection, or the whole page/artboard? And which system: Lyra (default) or SOL?
examples: Audit this page against Lyra and give me the compliance score.
Run a full audit on my selected frame and show the issues by category.
How compliant is this screen with SOL?

tools.name: lyra_compliance_report
tools.title: Lyra readiness report
tools.what: A full audit plus the accessibility pass, pinned to Lyra, formatted as a report rather than a raw issue dump.
tools.benefit: The artifact to paste into a design review or a ticket: score, gauge, and the top offenders, already prose.
examples: Write me a Lyra compliance report for this page.
Give me something I can share with my team about how Lyra-ready this screen is.
Produce a compliance report, not a raw issue dump.

tools.name: audit_colors
tools.title: Score the colors
tools.what: Classifies every fill and stroke as on-token, bound to the wrong design system, or a raw value with no binding.
tools.benefit: Tells you not just how many colors are off but how many are one click from being right, so you know whether this is ten minutes of work or a week.
examples: Which colors on this page are not Lyra tokens?
Check my fills and strokes for wrong-system or unbound colors.
How many of the color issues here can be fixed with one click?

tools.name: audit_text_styles
tools.title: Score the typography
tools.what: Matches every text node on family, size and weight together, and names the role-equivalent token it should be using.
tools.benefit: Catches the sneaky case (right size, wrong family) that eyeballing a design never finds.
examples: Do all the text nodes here match Lyra type tokens?
Which headings are using the wrong size or weight?
Find text that is close to a token but not quite on it.

tools.name: audit_spacing
tools.title: Score the spacing
tools.what: Finds padding, gap and margin values that are off-scale, or on-scale but not bound to a variable.
tools.benefit: Surfaces the "looks fine, breaks on theme change" class of problem, which is most of what fails in handoff.
examples: Find spacing that is off the Lyra scale.
Which paddings and gaps are on-scale but not bound to a variable?
Check the spacing in the selected frame.

tools.name: audit_radius
tools.title: Score the corner radii
tools.what: Finds corner radii that are off-scale or unbound, reading the real per-corner binding slots.
tools.benefit: Radius drift is the fastest way a page stops looking like the system. This is the cheapest audit to act on.
examples: Are my corner radii on the Lyra scale?
Find rounded corners that are not bound to a radius token.
Audit the border radius on this page.

tools.name: audit_components
tools.title: Score the components
tools.what: Finds instances from the wrong library or from no library, and names a 1:1 replacement where one exists.
tools.benefit: Detached and off-system components are what make a file un-maintainable. This is the list to fix first.
examples: Which instances in this file come from the wrong library?
Find components I should swap for the Lyra equivalent.
Audit the components in my selected frame.

tools.name: audit_accessibility
tools.title: Score accessibility
tools.what: WCAG-oriented scan: contrast, tap targets, small text, ARIA, alt text, labels, focus outlines, heading order, landmarks.
tools.benefit: Errors and warnings split out separately, so you can see what is a genuine blocker versus what is polish.
tools.ask: Want the fixable issues applied afterwards, or just the report?
examples: Check this page for accessibility problems.
Scan for contrast failures and tap targets that are too small.
Audit headings, landmarks, alt text and focus outlines on this screen.

tools.name: scan_variables
tools.title: List the variables in use
tools.what: Enumerates every variable currently bound in the scope, and every property that should be bound but is not.
tools.benefit: The raw data behind the spacing and radius scores, if you want to reason about bindings yourself.
examples: Which variables are bound in this frame, and what should be but is not?
List every property here that is missing a variable binding.
Show me the variable coverage for my selection.

tools.name: get_audit_filters
tools.title: See what the score ignores
tools.what: Returns the user's active audit filters: which issue classes are currently excluded from the score.
tools.benefit: Keeps the score honest. A 96 with contrast checks switched off is not a 96, and this is how you find out.
examples: Which issue types are currently excluded from my score?
Show me my active audit filters.
Why does my score look higher than I expected? Check the filters.

tools.name: set_audit_filters
tools.title: Change what the score ignores
tools.what: Turns individual issue classes in or out of scope for the score.
tools.benefit: Lets you park issues that are genuinely out of scope for this project without them nagging in every audit.
tools.ask: Which checks should be excluded, and should that stick for later audits too?
examples: Exclude spacing issues from my audit score.
Turn the radius checks back on.
Ignore component issues for now and keep that setting for next time.

tools.name: convert_page_to_lyra
tools.title: Convert the whole page to Lyra
tools.what: Runs every applicable fixer across a live page and returns a before/after score delta.
tools.benefit: The single biggest jump in score you can get in one call, and you see exactly how many points it bought.
tools.ask: Tokens-only (precise, keeps the layout, best for demos and finished work) or a full conversion (also normalises layout, components and a11y, best for early mockups)?
examples: Convert this page to Lyra, tokens only, and show me a dry run first.
Do a full Lyra conversion on this page and tell me how much the score moves.
What would converting this page to Lyra change? Do not apply anything yet.

tools.name: migrate_to_lyra
tools.title: Convert the whole frame to Lyra
tools.what: The Figma equivalent: applies the selected fixer families across a frame and reports the score delta.
tools.benefit: Migrates a whole artboard without hand-picking rows, with a before/after gauge to show your team.
tools.ask: Which families should run: colors, typography, spacing, radius, accessibility? And tokens-only or a full conversion?
examples: Migrate my selected frame to Lyra, colors and type only.
Run a dry-run Lyra migration on this artboard and show the score change.
Convert this frame to Lyra and keep the layout as it is.

tools.name: convert_colors
tools.title: Apply color tokens
tools.what: Binds the chosen color tokens to the listed fills and strokes.
tools.benefit: Reports how many of the original color issues it actually resolved, so a partial fix never gets reported as a win.
tools.ask: Apply every suggested color, or only the exact matches and leave the judgement calls to you?
examples: Bind every exact-match color to its Lyra token and leave the rest for me.
Convert the colors in this frame to Lyra, dry run first.
Apply all the suggested color tokens.

tools.name: convert_text_styles
tools.title: Apply typography tokens
tools.what: Applies the matching type token to the given text nodes, or to every eligible one.
tools.benefit: Type is the most visible domain: this is the change people notice, and it comes with a resolved-count.
tools.ask: All text nodes, or should any be skipped (logos and custom display type usually should)?
examples: Apply Lyra type tokens to all the text here except the logo.
Convert the text styles on this page, dry run first.
Which text nodes would change if you converted to Lyra type?

tools.name: fix_spacing
tools.title: Bind spacing tokens
tools.what: Binds spacing variables to off-scale or unbound padding, gap and margin values.
tools.benefit: Usually the highest-yield, lowest-risk fix in the set: values barely move, but the score does.
examples: Snap the off-scale spacing here to the nearest Lyra token.
Bind spacing variables to every unbound padding and gap in this frame.
Fix the spacing and tell me the before and after.

tools.name: fix_radius
tools.title: Bind radius tokens
tools.what: Binds radius variables to off-scale or unbound corner radii.
tools.benefit: Small visual change, large consistency gain, and it takes one call.
examples: Bind radius tokens to every corner that is off the scale.
Fix the border radius on this page and show me what changed.
Dry-run a radius fix on my selection.

tools.name: fix_accessibility
tools.title: Apply accessibility fixes
tools.what: Applies the automated remediation for a specific accessibility issue type on a node.
tools.benefit: Clears the mechanical a11y failures (labels, alt text, tap targets) so human attention goes to the judgement calls.
tools.ask: Auto-fixable issues only, or should we also attempt the ones that need judgement (contrast trade-offs, copy rewrites)?
examples: Fix the accessibility issues that can be fixed automatically.
Apply the contrast fix to this element.
Which a11y issues would you fix, and which need my judgement?

tools.name: convert_component
tools.title: Swap a component for its system twin
tools.what: Replaces one instance with the equivalent component from the target design system.
tools.benefit: Gets you a real library instance, inheriting future updates, instead of a look-alike that drifts.
tools.ask: Confirm the replacement component name before swapping, a wrong swap loses instance overrides.
examples: Swap this button for the Lyra button, and tell me the name first.
Replace the selected instance with its Lyra equivalent.
Is there a Lyra version of this component I can swap in?

tools.name: convert_mode
tools.title: Switch light / dark mode
tools.what: Re-binds the scope to the light or dark tokens of the given system.
tools.benefit: Produces a genuine dark variant built from tokens, not an inverted screenshot.
examples: Switch this frame to dark mode tokens.
Re-bind the selection to Lyra light mode.
Show me this screen in dark mode using the real tokens.

tools.name: generate_multi_system
tools.title: Duplicate into the other system
tools.what: Copies the selection and converts the copy to the other design system, leaving the original untouched.
tools.benefit: Side-by-side SOL and Lyra versions for a migration pitch, with zero risk to the original.
examples: Make a Lyra copy of this SOL screen next to the original.
Duplicate my selection and convert the copy to SOL.
Give me both design system versions of this frame side by side.

tools.name: apply_single_color
tools.title: Set one color
tools.what: Applies one color token (or a raw hex via customHex) to a single fill or stroke.
tools.benefit: Try a value in one call and undo it in one call. This is the lane for "just make this blue".
examples: Change just this fill to the Lyra primary color token.
Bind the selected stroke to the right border token.
Apply the hex #1A73E8 to this one fill.

tools.name: apply_single_text
tools.title: Set one text style
tools.what: Applies one type token (or a raw size via customFontSize) to a single text node.
tools.benefit: Iterate on one heading without touching the other forty.
examples: Make only this heading use the Lyra title token.
Apply the body type token to the selected text.
Set this one label to 14px.

tools.name: apply_single_spacing
tools.title: Set one spacing value
tools.what: Applies one spacing token (or a raw number via customValue) to a single property.
tools.benefit: Nudge one gap by hand when the token scale genuinely does not have the right step.
examples: Set this padding to the nearest Lyra spacing token.
Bind the gap on this frame to a spacing variable.
Change just this margin to 16.

tools.name: apply_single_radius
tools.title: Set one corner radius
tools.what: Applies one radius token (or a raw number via customValue) to a single corner or all four.
tools.benefit: Fix the one card whose corners are wrong, without a page-wide pass.
examples: Give this card the Lyra medium radius token.
Set all four corners on the selection to the same radius token.
Change just the top-left corner radius.

tools.name: revert_single_color
tools.title: Undo that one color
tools.what: Restores the snapshot captured when that exact fill or stroke was changed.
tools.benefit: Per-row undo that survives other edits, no losing four good changes to walk back a fifth.
examples: Undo the color change on that one fill.
Put the stroke back to what it was before.
Revert the last single color edit.

tools.name: revert_single_text
tools.title: Undo that one text style
tools.what: Restores the snapshot captured when that text node was changed.
tools.benefit: Try a type token, dislike it, put it back exactly as it was.
examples: Undo the type change on that heading.
Restore the original text style on the node I just changed.
Revert that one text edit.

tools.name: revert_single_spacing
tools.title: Undo that one spacing value
tools.what: Restores the snapshot captured when that spacing property was changed.
tools.benefit: Reverses a single nudge without disturbing the rest of the layout.
examples: Put that padding back the way it was.
Undo the spacing change on this frame.
Revert the last single spacing edit.

tools.name: revert_single_radius
tools.title: Undo that one corner radius
tools.what: Restores the snapshot captured when that radius was changed.
tools.benefit: Reverses a single radius edit cleanly.
examples: Undo the radius change on that card.
Restore the original corner radius.
Revert the last single radius edit.

tools.name: undo_last_conversion
tools.title: Undo the last bulk change
tools.what: Rolls back the most recent bulk conversion in one call.
tools.benefit: Lets you run a big conversion to see what it does, knowing the exit is one sentence away.
examples: Undo that last conversion.
That page conversion went wrong. Roll it back.
Take me back to before the bulk fix.

tools.name: get_conversion_history
tools.title: List every change made
tools.what: Returns the ordered history of applied changes with the current position in it.
tools.benefit: A written record of what this session actually touched, useful for a changelog or a handoff note.
examples: Show me everything we have changed so far.
List the history of applied conversions.
Where am I in the change history?

tools.name: revert_to_history_index
tools.title: Rewind to an earlier point
tools.what: Steps the design back to a chosen entry in the history.
tools.benefit: Explore aggressively, then land on whichever version was best, not just the last one.
tools.ask: Which history entry should we land on? Everything after it will be undone.
examples: Go back to the state after the second change.
Step the design back to history entry 3.
Undo everything after the color conversion but keep the color conversion.

tools.name: apply_css_overrides
tools.title: Inject CSS rules
tools.what: Injects selector-scoped CSS declarations into the live page.
tools.benefit: Restyle anything on a page you do not own, and see the result immediately. Pass clear:true so re-runs replace rather than stack.
tools.ask: Show the selector-to-declaration table and get a yes before injecting, a wrong selector can restyle the whole page.
examples: Try making the primary buttons on this page use the Lyra blue.
Inject a CSS override so the header uses the dark surface color.
Show me the selectors you would change, then apply them.

tools.name: clear_css_overrides
tools.title: Remove injected CSS
tools.what: Strips every override this session injected, returning the page to its shipped styling.
tools.benefit: A clean baseline in one call, so an experiment never contaminates the next audit.
examples: Remove all the CSS you injected.
Put the page back to how it shipped.
Clear the overrides and reload the original look.

tools.name: polish_page
tools.title: Page view toggles
tools.what: Toggles dark-mode simulation, token-styled scrollbars, and positional hover overlays.
tools.benefit: Dark mode without a build, on any page: the fastest way to find out what breaks.
examples: Turn on dark mode simulation for this page.
Show hover overlays and token-styled scrollbars.
Polish this page so it looks right for a demo.

tools.name: a11y_overlay
tools.title: Accessibility overlays
tools.what: Toggles small-tap-target highlighting, non-token color flagging, and colorblind simulation.
tools.benefit: Makes accessibility problems visible on screen, which is far more persuasive in a review than a list of counts.
examples: Highlight every tap target that is too small.
Simulate what this page looks like with deuteranopia.
Flag the colors on this page that are not tokens.

tools.name: extract_dev_details
tools.title: Spec sheet for one element
tools.what: Size, fills, strokes, typography, auto-layout and CSS for the current selection. On a figma.com tab, reads the real layer from Figma's API instead of the page.
tools.benefit: The handoff spec a developer asks for, without a screenshot-and-annotate round trip.
examples: Give me the dev specs for the element I selected.
What are the size, fills, type and layout for this layer?
I need the CSS for this button. What is it?

tools.name: extract_all_css
tools.title: Export the whole thing as CSS
tools.what: Emits a CSS document covering every node in scope.
tools.benefit: A real starting point for implementation rather than a pile of values to retype.
examples: Export the CSS for everything in this frame.
Give me one CSS document for the whole selection.
Generate CSS I can hand to a developer for this screen.

tools.name: extract_token_css
tools.title: Export CSS custom properties
tools.what: Emits the design system's tokens as CSS custom properties.
tools.benefit: Drop it into a stylesheet and the rest of the exported CSS resolves against real tokens.
examples: Give me the Lyra tokens as CSS custom properties.
Export the SOL design tokens as CSS variables.
I need the dark mode token CSS for Lyra.

tools.name: export_design_tokens
tools.title: Export the token palettes
tools.what: Returns the color, type, spacing and radius palettes for SOL or Lyra in either mode.
tools.benefit: Lets Claude propose real token names instead of guessing at them from memory.
examples: Export the full Lyra color and type palette.
Give me the SOL spacing and radius tokens as data.
Show me the Lyra dark mode colors.

tools.name: sync_storybook_components
tools.title: Sync components from Storybook
tools.what: Pulls the live component inventory from a Storybook instance into the plugin.
tools.benefit: Component audits start matching what engineering actually shipped, not last quarter's library.
tools.ask: Which Storybook URL, and should this replace the current inventory or merge into it?
examples: Sync the components from our Storybook.
Pull the latest Lyra component list from Storybook into the plugin.
Refresh the component inventory, replacing what is there.

tools.name: get_storybook_sync_status
tools.title: Storybook sync status
tools.what: Reports when the last sync ran and how many components it brought in.
tools.benefit: Tells you whether a component audit is trustworthy or built on stale data.
examples: When did Storybook last sync?
How many components did the last sync bring in?
Is my component inventory up to date?

tools.name: check_for_updates
tools.title: Check for a newer server build
tools.what: Fetches origin and reports whether the local MCP server checkout is behind, with the commit list and version numbers.
tools.benefit: Know there is an update before running it, instead of finding out a feature is missing after the fact.
examples: Is my NiCE Designer connector up to date?
Check whether there are new commits for the MCP server.
What would I get if I updated the connector?

tools.name: install_update
tools.title: Pull and install the latest build
tools.what: Fast-forwards the local checkout to origin and runs npm install for whatever changed. Only works from a git checkout, and only when the working tree is clean.
tools.benefit: Gets new tools and fixes onto disk in one call, though the running process still needs a restart to actually load them, which the response always states.
tools.ask: Show the pending commits (from check_for_updates or a dry run) and confirm before running with dryRun:false.
examples: Show me the pending updates, then install them.
Update the local MCP server to the latest version.
Pull in the newest changes and run npm install.

tools.name: reinstall_connector
tools.title: Reinstall the Claude Connector
tools.what: Relaunches the "Click to install Claude Connector.mcpb" file via the OS's own handler, same as double-clicking it. Only works from a git checkout or the unpacked Chrome folder, not from a Desktop-managed install.
tools.benefit: No hunting for the file yourself when a tool/skill update needs a reinstall, though Desktop's own confirm dialog is still the last step.
tools.ask: Confirm the person wants to relaunch the installer before running with dryRun:false, since it hands off to Claude Desktop's own install flow.
examples: My connector is out of date. Relaunch the installer.
Reinstall the NiCE Designer connector for me.
The Supercharge page says to reinstall. Do that.

tools.name: call_plugin
tools.title: Send a raw plugin message
tools.what: Forwards any raw UIMessage straight to the plugin, bypassing the typed tools.
tools.benefit: Reaches plugin capability that has no tool yet. Powerful, unvalidated: use it when nothing else fits.
tools.ask: Confirm the exact message payload first; this path has no dry-run and no schema validation.
examples: Send this raw message to the plugin and show me what comes back.
None of the tools cover this. Call the plugin directly.
Forward a custom UIMessage to Figma.

skills.title: Accessibility triage
skills.question: I have hundreds of a11y issues, where do I actually start?
skills.what: Ranks accessibility issues by severity × reach and returns a top-N action list.
skills.benefit: Converts an unreadable issue dump into three things to fix this afternoon.
examples: I have hundreds of accessibility issues on this page. Where do I start?
Triage the a11y issues here and give me the top 10 to fix first.
Which accessibility problems affect the most users?

skills.title: Manual-fixes checklist
skills.question: What is left for a human after the auto-fixers have run?
skills.what: Audits, dry-runs every fixer, then reports only what survives, grouped and prioritised.
skills.benefit: An honest to-do list for the last mile to 100%, so nobody promises a score the tools cannot reach.
examples: What is left for me to fix by hand after the auto-fixers run?
Dry-run every fixer and list only what still needs a human.
Make me a manual fixes checklist for this page.

skills.title: Lyra visual patterns
skills.question: What is a correctly-converted Lyra page supposed to look like?
skills.what: Reference for Lyra page chrome, surfaces, tables, panels, nav, chips and AI affordances in light and dark.
skills.benefit: Load it before any conversion and you know what you are going to get, no surprise redesigns.
examples: What should a correctly converted Lyra page look like?
Load the Lyra visual patterns before we convert this screen.
How should Lyra tables, panels and chips look in dark mode?

skills.title: Figma element → CSS
skills.question: What is the CSS for this layer?
skills.what: Turns the selected Figma node into production CSS with Lyra tokens substituted where they match.
skills.benefit: Output that survives a theme change, instead of hard-coded hex and px.
examples: What is the CSS for this layer?
Turn the selected Figma node into production CSS with Lyra tokens.
Write CSS for this card using token variables wherever they match.

skills.title: Browser element → spec sheet
skills.question: What are the design specs of this element on the page?
skills.what: Pulls computed CSS for the inspected element and annotates every raw value with its nearest token.
skills.benefit: A spec a developer can act on, not just a description of what is there.
examples: What are the design specs for the element I inspected?
Annotate every raw value on this element with its nearest token.
Give me a spec sheet for this button.

skills.title: Figma ↔ Chrome parity
skills.question: Does the live site actually match the Figma?
skills.what: Aligns Figma layers to page elements by name and diffs colors, type, spacing, radius and shadows.
skills.benefit: Ends the "it looks off but I cannot say why" review with a per-property drift table.
examples: Does the live site actually match the Figma?
Diff this artboard against the page that implements it.
Find every place the build drifted from the design in color, type and spacing.

skills.title: Artboard → live page
skills.question: Can we make this real page look like this artboard?
skills.what: Maps artboard styling onto page selectors and applies it as CSS overrides after you confirm the mapping.
skills.benefit: Demo a redesign on the real product in minutes, with no branch and no build.
examples: Make this live page look like my selected artboard.
Show me the mapping from artboard layers to page selectors before applying.
Push the artboard styling onto the page as CSS overrides.

skills.title: Dark-mode parity
skills.question: Does this page work in dark mode, or only in light?
skills.what: Audits colors in light, simulates dark, audits again, and always restores the baseline.
skills.benefit: Only the delta: what breaks in dark and what breaks in light. No re-reading the full audit.
examples: Does this page work in dark mode?
Audit the colors in light, then dark, and tell me what breaks.
Check dark mode parity and put the page back how it was.

skills.title: Token candidates
skills.question: Which of these custom values should just become Lyra tokens?
skills.what: Groups recurring raw values across all four domains and ranks the ones worth promoting.
skills.benefit: Fixes the cause once upstream instead of the same symptom on thirty screens.
examples: Which of these custom values should become Lyra tokens?
Find recurring raw values on this page worth promoting.
Rank the custom colors and spacing we use most often.

skills.title: NiCE product knowledge
skills.question: What does this NICE product actually do, and who uses it?
skills.what: Sourced reference on NICE the company and its product lines (CXone Mpower, Enlighten AI, Actimize, Evidencentral), compiled from public material with citations.
skills.benefit: Design decisions grounded in what the real product and its real users are, instead of generic SaaS assumptions.
examples: What does Enlighten AI actually do and who uses it?
Give me background on CXone Mpower before I design for it.
Which NICE product line does this feature belong to?

skills.title: Team strengths
skills.question: Who should I put on this, and what will this group get wrong?
skills.what: The design team's CliftonStrengths grid (45 people, top 10 themes each) plus the analysis: lookup, group composition, find-the-person matching, and 1:1 coaching prep.
skills.benefit: Staffing and 1:1 decisions grounded in how people actually work, instead of who was free.
examples: What are the top strengths for the people on my team?
Who should I staff on this project, and what will the group be missing?
Help me prep a strengths-based 1:1 with someone.

skills.title: Install or update NiCE Designer
skills.question: Can Claude install or update the NiCE Designer extension for me?
skills.what: Asks clean install or update, downloads the latest release, unzips it to a permanent folder, opens the extensions page and clicks through Load unpacked with computer use when allowed, otherwise guides each step.
skills.benefit: Gets a person from nothing to a verified working install without hunting for the zip, and hands them the site, install guide and password.
examples: Install the NiCE Designer Suite for me.
Update my NiCE Designer extension to the latest version.
Do a clean reinstall of NiCE Designer.

skills.title: Prompt guru
skills.question: Is this prompt actually going to get me what I want?
skills.what: Reviews a vague or under-specified prompt, rewrites it, explains the improvement, and runs the better version.
skills.benefit: Catches ambiguity before it burns a turn on the wrong answer.
examples: Is this prompt going to get me what I want?
Rewrite this vague prompt so it works better and explain what you changed.
Improve my prompt and run the better version.

skills.title: UI bug hunter
skills.question: What is wrong with this screenshot?
skills.what: Runs a structured 9-layer visual QA pass over a screenshot, image, or recording and produces Jira-style tickets for every real issue.
skills.benefit: A bug list ready to file, not a paragraph of impressions.
examples: What is wrong with this screenshot?
Do a visual QA pass on this build and write Jira tickets for what you find.
Review this screen recording for UI bugs.

skills.title: Lyra UI prototyping
skills.question: Can Claude build a working prototype from the real Lyra components, at 100% Lyra, and tell me what Lyra cannot do yet?
skills.what: The official skill for coded prototypes. Builds a real, clickable prototype (React first, Angular where React has no component) from the actual Lyra components in the Storybook the plugin syncs, holds it to 100% Lyra tokens and components, audits the live page in Chrome until it scores 100, and ships a GAPS.md listing everything Lyra does not have.
skills.benefit: A demo that is actually Lyra, proven by a live audit score, plus an honest list of what is missing instead of look-alikes standing in for it.
examples: Build a clickable prototype of this screen from the real Lyra components.
Prototype this flow in React at 100 percent Lyra and tell me what Lyra is missing.
Code up a working demo of this admin page and audit it until it scores 100.

skills.title: SOL UI prototyping
skills.question: Can Claude build a working prototype from the real SOL components and tell me what SOL cannot do yet?
skills.what: Builds a real coded prototype (React first, Angular where React has no component) from the SOL component library, holds it to full SOL adherence, audits the live page in Chrome, and ships a GAPS.md listing everything SOL does not have.
skills.benefit: A demo that is actually SOL, plus an honest, rechecked list of what is missing instead of look-alikes standing in for it.
examples: Build a clickable prototype of this screen from real SOL components.
Prototype this flow in React with SOL and tell me what SOL is missing.
Make this demo 100 percent SOL and list the gaps.

skills.title: Claude Design prompt from audit
skills.question: Can the audit results become a prompt I paste into Claude Design?
skills.what: Runs the audits, groups the issues into the changes a designer would make (token swaps, type, spacing, components, accessibility), and writes one ready-to-paste Claude Design prompt.
skills.benefit: Hand the audit to a generative design tool as a brief it can act on, with real token names and an accessibility floor, instead of fixing the page by hand.
examples: Turn the audit results for this page into a Claude Design prompt.
Write me a prompt I can paste into Claude Design to fix this screen in Lyra.
Audit this frame and give me a design brief for Claude Design, accessibility first.

skills.title: Design system agent
skills.question: Can Claude keep fixing this page until it’s actually 100% SOL/Lyra compliant, not just close?
skills.what: Builds or edits a Claude Code project’s UI using only real SOL/Lyra Storybook components, then loops audit → fix-in-source → re-audit against the live page in Chrome until it hits your compliance target.
skills.benefit: A screen that’s provably on-system by the numbers, not eyeballed, and every fix lands in your source, not a throwaway DOM patch.
examples: Keep fixing this page until it hits 95 percent Lyra compliance.
Build this screen from real Lyra Storybook components and audit it live.
Loop audit, fix and re-audit on my dev server until the score holds.

skills.title: Maya Chen — New agent
skills.question: How would someone brand-new to CXone react to this?
skills.what: A three-weeks-in contact center agent, mid-call attention and no admin context — starter archetype, not yet sourced from a real study.
skills.benefit: Catches onboarding friction, jargon, and cognitive load a confident reviewer would miss.
examples: Interview Maya about this new onboarding flow.
How would a brand-new agent react to this screen mid-call?
Ask a first-week agent whether this is too much to figure out on the fly.

skills.title: Jordan Reyes — Supervisor
skills.question: Would this slow down real-time team monitoring?
skills.what: A frontline supervisor running 14 agents, triaging live dashboards between interruptions — starter archetype, not yet sourced from a real study.
skills.benefit: Grounds a review in real-time, SLA-driven operational reality instead of an assumed power user.
examples: Ask a supervisor whether this dashboard change helps during a live shift.
Interview Jordan about this real-time monitoring redesign.
Would this slow down a supervisor triaging SLA breaches?

skills.title: Patricia Odom — Executive
skills.question: What is the VP pitch for this, and would leadership actually fund it?
skills.what: A VP of Customer Experience who sponsors CXone but rarely opens it herself, judging everything by outcome and cost of inaction — starter archetype, not yet sourced from a real study.
skills.benefit: Pressure-tests a pitch against a non-technical executive sponsor before it reaches one for real.
examples: What is the VP pitch for this feature?
Interview an executive sponsor about whether this is worth funding.
Would leadership actually approve this, or does it need a different pitch?

skills.title: Sam Whitfield — Coach
skills.question: Would this actually help someone coaching agents?
skills.what: A quality/performance coach who reviews calls and runs developmental 1:1s, judging tools by whether they give something actionable to tell an agent — starter archetype, not yet sourced from a real study.
skills.benefit: Checks a feature against a coaching/feedback-loop lens instead of a real-time-ops or executive one.
examples: Ask a coach whether this scorecard change actually helps them coach.
Interview Sam about this quality-monitoring feature.
Would this give a coach something concrete to tell an agent?
